title: Tensor compatibility with restricted coefficient quotient transitions
statement:
Fix a universe $u$, a prime $\ell$, a finite-dimensional extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a scheme $X$ in universe $u$, a finite-field datum $D$, and $\ell\ne D.p$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. On the small pro-etale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] let $B$ be the completed integral coefficient ring and $B_n$ its quotient of exponent $n+1$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $F_n:D(B)\to D(B_n)$ for derived extension and $U_n:D(B_n)\to D(B)$ for derived restriction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction, def-weil-integral-derived-restriction-of-scalars], and $\tau_n:U_{n+1}F_{n+1}\to U_nF_n$ for the canonical quotient transition [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. Fix an ordinary tensor presentation $a$ and normalized reduction presentations $m_n$ with tensor comparisons $\mu_n:F_nT\simeq T_n(F_n,F_n)$ [def-sf-integral-hom-reduction-models]. For arbitrary $K,V\in D(B)$, construct $b_n(K,V):T(K,U_nF_nV)\to U_nF_nT(K,V)$ as the scalar-adjunction transpose of the composite $\mu_n(K,U_nF_nV)$ followed by $T_n(1,\epsilon_{F_nV})$ followed by $\mu_n(K,V)^{-1}$, where $\epsilon$ is the actual scalar-adjunction counit. Then
$$T(1,\tau_n(V));b_n(K,V)=b_{n+1}(K,V);\tau_n(T(K,V))$$
for every $n\in\mathbf N$. No Hom, dualizing object, invertible Hom comparison, completeness, constructibility or boundedness hypothesis occurs.

proof.text: Construct the scalar tensor mates as a natural transformation in the pair of derived inputs, using the unit, normalized tensor comparison, and scalar counit. This is tensorMate and tensorMate_app.

Use ordinaryTensorQuotient_contractions for chain maps with their pure-section formula and quotient square. On K-flat representatives P,Q, use restrictionTensor_mate_model separately at the two levels; the same natural isomorphism e occurs at both levels.

The representative equation of sfDerivedReductionTransition applies to Q and T(P,Q), which is K-flat by coefficientTotalTensor_isKFlat. The private transportTransition diagram calculation uses naturality of e and the derived transition to transport the ordinary quotient square, then cancels the representative comparison isomorphism and e.

Apply the existing sfDerived_natTrans_ext to whiskerings of the two composite natural transformations, first with the second input fixed at a K-flat representative, and then with the first input arbitrary. That proved helper uses K-flat resolutions, naturality and cancellation of localization isomorphisms. Component extensionality gives equality of the two transformations, hence the square for arbitrary K and V.

lean.statement:
theorem restrictionTensor_transition
    (a : TensorPresentation.{u, u} X (completedIntegralCommRingSheaf l E X D hl))
    (m : ∀ n : ℕ, ReductionPresentation l E X D hl a n)
    (K V : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E X)) (n : ℕ) :
    a.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 K) ((sfDerivedReductionTransition l E X n).app V)) ≫
        restrictionTensor l E X D hl (m n) K V =
      restrictionTensor l E X D hl (m (n + 1)) K V ≫
        (sfDerivedReductionTransition l E X n).app (a.tensor.obj (K, V))
